title: France’s Election And The Law Of Surprise
text:
France’s Election And The Law Of Surprise

Cedric Gemehl

Gavekal Research | 26 Nov 2026

One of the biggest political events for European assets in 2027 will be France’s presidential election, with the first and second rounds scheduled for April 18 and May 2. Five months ahead of the election, opinion polls point to a run-off between Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, with Le Pen enjoying a commanding lead in second-round polling.Recent polls put Le Pen at around 33% of first-round voting intentions, with Mélenchon a distant second at 18%. Both are well ahead of former center-right prime minister Édouard Philippe and center-left candidate Raphaël Glucksmann, each polling around 11%. In a hypothetical run-off against Mélenchon, Le Pen polls at around 68%.
